historical_record.description: Recorded in the city's 2008 survey of the Transit Center District, adopted in 2012, as a contributor to the proposed New Montgomery, Mission & Second Historic District.
Its shell was among the handful in the district left standing after the April 1906 earthquake and fire.
The 1917 Crocker-Langley city directory lists the offices of Oscar Hudson, an African American attorney, in the Monadnock Building here.

unknowns: The inventory table in the same report dates this building to 1906, the year of the earthquake it describes the building as having survived.
